 Updated October 23, 13:25 UTC: The PHP project has disclosed a third vulnerability, CVE-2026-115560 . Every Hostinger hosting plan except VPS is already fully protected by the changes we made on October 21, so no action is needed. PHP will include a fix in its next regular release, and we’ll roll it out as part of normal maintenance. If you run PHP on a VPS, set session.upload_progress.enabled = Off in php.ini or your PHP-FPM pool config and restart all PHP workers (see step 2 below). If you already did this on October 21, you’re covered. Live updates are on our status page .
 Updated October 22, 07:20 UTC: PHP’s fix is now installed on all Hostinger hosting servers except VPS, which customers manage themselves. For live status, see our status page .
 On October 21, the PHP project fixed two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, now known as php2shell. Both are rated 9.2 out of 10 on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). Details leaked before the planned release, and exploit code for one of them was already circulating before the fix was out. We blocked the exploit attempts already circulating in advance, and we’ve rolled out PHP’s update across our platform. 
 In short: 
 Every Hostinger hosting plan except VPS: nothing to do. We manage PHP on these plans and have taken care of it: the circulating exploit did not work against our servers, our firewall rules blocked requests that match the attack, and we’ve installed PHP’s fix on every server.
 VPS: if you manage PHP on your own server, update it and restart it now. The steps are below.
 What we know about the vulnerabilities 
 Both bugs come down to how PHP cleans up memory when a request goes wrong. In the worst case, an attacker could run their own code on a server, read data they shouldn’t see, or take a site down.
 Vulnerability What goes wrong 
 CVE-2026-109618 A request pushes PHP to its memory limit at exactly the wrong moment. PHP stops halfway, leaves some data half-built, and later treats it as if it were complete. 
 CVE-2026-109619 An error interrupts a request, and PHP holds onto memory that has already been freed. The next request handled by the same process can then reach that leftover memory. 
 Every PHP version before 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 is affected, going back at least to PHP 5.4. That covers WordPress, WooCommerce, Magento, and most other PHP sites.
 Because the flaw is in PHP itself, updating WordPress, themes, or plugins won’t fix it. Only a patched PHP does.
 What we’ve done 
 First, we blocked the attacks already doing the rounds. We added security rules that catch known exploit patterns and updated our firewall rule set, which reaches every server running ModSecurity automatically. The rules run in deny mode, so any matching request is rejected by the server immediately.
 We also switched off session.upload_progress on our LiteSpeed, PHP Selector and cPanel PHP-FPM setups, and on phpMyAdmin. Hardly any sites use this feature, and turning it off closes one known route to CVE-2026-109619. On our web hosting platform, we now reject malformed upload requests that PHP could misread.
 Once PHP released versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, we rolled them out across the platform (completed October 22 at 06:44 UTC) and emailed customers to let them know. On managed hosting, the fix is built into the PHP version your site already runs, so the version number may not change. To check, open Hostinger dashboard → Websites → Dashboard → PHP Info. A Build Date of October 21, 2026 or later means your site has the fix.
 We have not seen any increase in malware infections or unusual activity on our managed hosting since the vulnerabilities became public.
 We continue monitoring traffic closely and will adjust our rules if attackers change tactics.
 What you need to do 
 Every Hostinger hosting plan except VPS : nothing. We manage PHP for you, and the fix has been installed automatically. You can check the status here .
 If you run PHP yourself on VPS :
 On a VPS server that is running PHP, you manage PHP yourself, so our server-level protections don’t apply. Act now:
 Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 as soon as you can. It’s the only complete fix.
 Can’t update straight away? Set session.upload_progress.enabled = Off in php.ini or your PHP-FPM pool config, then restart all PHP workers. Setting it in your code with ini_set won’t work. This closes one of the two php2shell bugs and fully protects against CVE-2026-115560, announced on October 23. When PHP ships the fix for the latter, update as part of your normal maintenance.
 Turn off uploads you don’t need and keep upload size limits reasonable. It lowers your risk, but it isn’t a substitute for updating.
 A few things that apply to everyone: 
 PHP 8.1 and older versions no longer get fixes from the PHP project, but sites on them are still covered on our managed hosting. The same protections we have apply to every PHP version. Agency hosting already runs patched builds of every version it offers, and patched builds are now deployed for every version from 5.2 to 8.5 on Web, Cloud, and cPanel hosting.
 Still, now is a good time to upgrade. Older versions miss many other security fixes, and PHP 8.2 stops getting security fixes on 31 Dec 2026. To upgrade your PHP version , go to the Hostinger dashboard → Websites → Dashboard → PHP Configuration and pick 8.3 or newer. Check that your theme and plugins support the new version first; if something breaks, you can switch back within the same login session.
 Why you still need the PHP update 
 Firewall rules are a safety net. They stop the attacks we already know about, but attackers keep tweaking their requests to slip past them. The PHP update fixes the actual bug, so we treat the two as a pair: the update for the fix, the rules for extra cover.
 Questions about your site? Our Customer Success team is available 24/7 via live chat in the Hostinger dashboard.
